name: Jayne Cronlund

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says she would start addressing housing by working with the Portland Housing Bureau to hold nonprofit partners accountable.
positions.excerpt: I would start addressing this by working with Portland Housing Bureau (PHB) to hold our nonprofit partners accountable

positions.statement: Willamette Week reported in its October 2026 endorsement that Cronlund focused on making sure the Portland Housing Bureau holds affordable housing organizations accountable for keeping their buildings safe and clean.
positions.excerpt: making sure the Portland Housing Bureau holds affordable housing organizations' feet to the fire

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune candidate Q&A, Cronlund says tangible progress toward goals such as reducing homelessness is unclear despite voters approving tax measures.
positions.excerpt: Tangible progress toward goals like reducing homelessness are murky despite voters approving tax measures.

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says a city's ultimate safety comes from a strong social fabric and not a police state.
positions.excerpt: A city’s ultimate safety comes from a strong social fabric and not a police state.

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says she would propose a step-by-step increase in the number of police officers.
positions.excerpt: I would propose stairstepping our way to increase police officers

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says the city will need to balance supporting job creation with neighborhood and climate impacts.
positions.excerpt: We will need to strike a balance between supporting this job creation and neighborhood and climate impacts.

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund describes small business owners as an integral, creative force in the city.
positions.excerpt: Small business owners are an integral, creative force in this City.

positions.statement: Willamette Week reported in its October 2026 endorsement that Cronlund described a vision focused on reviving empty storefronts.
positions.excerpt: Cronlund, 57, articulated a compelling and specific vision focused on reviving empty storefronts

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says she would create an online guide showing people where their property tax dollars go.
positions.excerpt: I will create an online guide for people to understand where their property tax dollars go

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune candidate Q&A, Cronlund says the tax burden on income earners is among the highest nationally.
positions.excerpt: The tax burden on income earners is nationally among the highest.

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund states that the cost of living in Portland is 19% higher than the national average.
positions.excerpt: The cost of living in Portland is 19% higher than the national average.

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says Portland residents need living wage jobs in order to thrive.
positions.excerpt: Portland citizens need living wage jobs in order to thrive

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune candidate Q&A, Cronlund says the city's aging infrastructure requires significant investments.
positions.excerpt: Our aging infrastructure requires significant investments.

positions.statement: On the plan page of her campaign site, Cronlund says she would provide a one-page, easy-to-read annual report as part of building trust in city officials.
positions.excerpt: I will provide a one-page, easy-to-read annual report

positions.statement: In a Portland Mercury candidate profile, Cronlund says she will be a voice for essential services, fiscal transparency and rebuilding trust with citizens.
positions.excerpt: I will be a voice for focusing on essential services, improving fiscal transparency and rebuilding trust with citizens.
